title: Hello, World
description: Print the classic greeting to the console: Hello, World!
hint: Put the exact text inside System.out.println("…"); and end the line with a semicolon.

title: Is it even?
description: Print true if the number n is even, or false if it is odd.
hint: n % 2 is the remainder after dividing by 2. Store n % 2 == 0 in a boolean and print it.

title: Sum of two numbers
description: Read two whole numbers with the Scanner and print their sum.
hint: Call in.nextInt() twice, store each number in an int variable, then print the two added together.

title: Largest of three
description: Print the biggest of the three numbers a, b and c.
hint: Start with int largest = a; then use one if to check b and another to check c.

title: Sum from 1 to n
hint: Keep a total that starts at 0, and add i to it on each pass of a for loop that counts from 1 to n.

title: Reverse a string
description: Print the characters of text in reverse order.
hint: Loop i from text.length() - 1 down to 0, and add text.charAt(i) to a new String each time.

title: Count above the target
description: Print how many numbers in the array nums are greater than target.
hint: Keep a count that starts at 0. Go through the array with a for loop and add 1 whenever a value is bigger than target.

title: Hypotenuse
description: a and b are the two short sides of a right triangle. Print the long side: the square root of a × a + b × b.
hint: Math.sqrt(x) returns the square root of x. Work out a * a + b * b first, then pass it to Math.sqrt and print the result.

title: Power, recursively
description: Fill in power so it returns base raised to exp (exp is 0 or more) by calling itself, without a loop.
hint: Base case: any number to the power 0 is 1. General case: base to the exp is base * power(base, exp - 1).

title: Box volume
description: Fill in the Box class: keep the length, width and height in private fields, set them in the constructor, and return length × width × height from volume().
hint: Declare three private int fields, copy each constructor parameter into its field with this.length = length; and so on, then multiply them in volume().

title: Shape areas
description: Square and Rect both extend the abstract class Shape. Fill in their area() methods so each shape returns its own area.
hint: A square's area is side * side, and a rectangle's is width * height. main stores each one as a Shape and calls area(), and Java picks the right version for you.

example.input: Shape[] shapes = { new Square(3), new Rect(2, 5) };

hidden.input: Shape[] shapes = { new Rect(4, 4), new Square(10), new Rect(1, 7) };
Shape[] shapes = { new Rect(0, 9), new Square(6) };

title: Score check
description: Fill in checkScore so it throws an InvalidScoreException when the score is below 0 or above 100, and does nothing for a valid score.
hint: Use an if with || to spot a bad score, then throw new InvalidScoreException("…"); main catches it and prints Invalid score.

title: Weekend or weekday
description: Fill in isWeekend so it returns true for SATURDAY and SUNDAY, and false for every other Day.
hint: Use a switch on day with a case for SATURDAY and SUNDAY that returns true, and return false otherwise. Comparing with == works too.

title: Student ID check
description: A student ID is two capital letters, a dash, then four digits, like AB-1234. Fill in isStudentId so it returns true only for IDs in that form.
hint: [A-Z] matches one capital letter and \d one digit, and {2} or {4} repeats the thing before it. Pass the pattern to id.matches(…).

title: Last of anything
description: Fill in the generic method lastOf so it returns the last item of any array, whether it holds words or numbers.
hint: The <T> before the return type lets the method work with any type. The last item sits at index items.length - 1.
